title: ⚖️ Advantages & Disadvantages Essays

sections.heading: Two question types — different structures
sections.body:
TYPE 1: "Discuss the advantages and disadvantages."
→ Write about both sides equally. Give your opinion only if asked.

TYPE 2: "Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?"
→ You MUST decide which side is stronger and argue for it. Don't sit on the fence.

Mixing these up costs you Task Achievement marks.

sections.heading: Structure for Type 1 (balanced)
sections.body:
Introduction: Paraphrase + state that there are both benefits and drawbacks
Body 1: Advantages (2 with development)
Body 2: Disadvantages (2 with development)
Conclusion: Summarise balance + opinion if asked

sections.heading: Structure for Type 2 (outweigh)
sections.body:
Introduction: Paraphrase + state your position (advantages/disadvantages outweigh)
Body 1: The side you think WINS (develop fully — 2 points)
Body 2: The other side (acknowledge — 1–2 points)
Conclusion: Restate your position firmly

highlight: For "outweigh" questions: your conclusion must match your introduction. If you say advantages outweigh in the intro, you CANNOT say it depends in the conclusion.

example.wrong: Technology has many advantages such as speed and communication. However, it also has disadvantages like addiction. In conclusion, technology is both good and bad.
example.right: While technology presents genuine risks — particularly regarding digital dependency and privacy erosion — I firmly contend that its capacity to democratise access to information and accelerate scientific progress constitutes a net benefit to society.

title: 🏗️ Developing Arguments — Not Just Listing
body:
Band 6 mistake: listing many points briefly
Band 8 technique: developing 2 points deeply

The PEEL structure:
Point: State your advantage/disadvantage
Explanation: Why is this an advantage/disadvantage?
Evidence: Give a specific example or data
Link: Connect back to the essay question

❌ Band 6: "Technology has many advantages: speed, communication, access to information, convenience and entertainment."
✅ Band 8: "Perhaps the most significant advantage of technology is its capacity to equalise access to education. Students in rural regions who previously had no access to quality teaching can now access university-level courses through online platforms — a transformation that has measurable impact on social mobility."

quick.label: 2 points fully developed beats 5 points mentioned

question: A question asks: "Do the advantages of working from home outweigh the disadvantages?" Which introduction is BEST?
options: Working from home has advantages and disadvantages which I will discuss.
There are many people who work from home nowadays.

While remote working presents challenges regarding collaboration and work-life boundaries, I contend that its benefits — particularly enhanced productivity and reduced commuting costs — ultimately represent a superior arrangement for most knowledge workers.
Working from home is very popular and has both good and bad sides.
correct: While remote working presents challenges regarding collaboration and work-life boundaries, I contend that its benefits — particularly enhanced productivity and reduced commuting costs — ultimately represent a superior arrangement for most knowledge workers.
explanation:
✅ Best introduction:
• "While..." = acknowledges the other side (shows balance)
• "I contend that" = clear position statement
• "ultimately represent a superior arrangement" = directly answers "outweigh"
• Specific examples: "productivity", "reduced commuting costs"
• "most knowledge workers" = appropriately hedged

❌ Others: vague, no position stated, or announce rather than argue

instruction: Match each essay element to its purpose in an advantages/disadvantages essay:

pairs.meaning: Acknowledges the weaker side with 1–2 points
States which side you believe is stronger
States the main idea of each body paragraph

explanation: All four elements are essential for Band 7+ advantages/disadvantages essays. The concession paragraph in particular shows academic maturity — you acknowledge the other side rather than ignoring it.

title: Find the Task Achievement Error
instruction: One paragraph makes a Task Achievement error:

sentences.text: Although technology offers clear educational benefits, I believe its social drawbacks — particularly the erosion of face-to-face communication — ultimately tip the balance against unrestricted adoption.
In conclusion, technology has both advantages and disadvantages, so it depends on the situation and how it is used by different people in different contexts.
sentences.explanation:
This conclusion fails Task Achievement for an "outweigh" question.

"It depends" = no clear position = Task Achievement penalty

✅ Correct: "In conclusion, while technology presents genuine risks, I maintain that its transformative benefits to education and communication decisively outweigh its drawbacks, provided appropriate safeguards are implemented."

sentences.text: One major advantage of globalisation is its capacity to reduce poverty through increased trade and foreign investment, as evidenced by the dramatic decline in extreme poverty in Southeast Asia since the 1990s.

question: Which body paragraph is closest to Band 8 for an advantages essay?
options: Technology is good because it helps people. For example, smartphones are useful.
One advantage of technology is communication. People can talk to others easily.

Perhaps the most transformative advantage of modern technology lies in its democratisation of access to knowledge. Learners in underserved regions — who previously had no access to quality educational resources — can now enrol in university-level courses through digital platforms, a shift that directly challenges entrenched cycles of educational inequality.
Technology has many advantages including speed, convenience, entertainment, education and communication, which are all very important for modern life.
correct: Perhaps the most transformative advantage of modern technology lies in its democratisation of access to knowledge. Learners in underserved regions — who previously had no access to quality educational resources — can now enrol in university-level courses through digital platforms, a shift that directly challenges entrenched cycles of educational inequality.
explanation:
✅ Band 8 features:
• "Perhaps the most transformative" = strong, specific claim
• "democratisation of access to knowledge" = sophisticated noun phrase
• "underserved regions" = precise vocabulary
• Specific mechanism: enrol in university-level courses via digital platforms
• "directly challenges entrenched cycles of educational inequality" = connects to broader significance

One fully developed example > five shallow points.
